title: CVE-2026-76519: Critical Cisco Secure Email Gateway Zero-Day Exploited for Root Access
content_md: Cisco has patched CVE-2026-76519, a critical zero-day vulnerability affecting Cisco Secure Email Gateway (SEG) that is already being exploited in real-world attacks. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and enables an unauthenticated remote attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on vulnerable appliances. The vulnerability resides in the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) functionality of Cisco Secure Email Gateway and stems from improper handling of email attachments when the File Reputation service is enabled. An attacker can exploit the issue simply by sending an email containing a specially crafted attachment through an affected gateway, without needing credentials or user interaction. Cisco disclosed the vulnerability on October 14, 2026, after its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) became aware of active exploitation during October. The company has not disclosed who is behind the attacks, how many appliances have been compromised, or what attackers have done after obtaining access. The vulnerability is especially concerning because Secure Email Gateway appliances are positioned directly in enterprise email infrastructure. Successful compromise with root privileges can provide attackers with extensive control over the security appliance, access to credentials and cryptographic material, and potentially a pathway toward additional systems.
